# What a foreign call costs is the half of a foreign declaration SNGL cannot
# read off the body: the body describes the foreign function rather than
# implementing it. `const func` and the flags on #[foreign] say it.

# const lets the compiler evaluate the call at build time — the result is in
# the markup and the function is gone.
sngl generate --lang=none --platform=html --out=pure pure.sngl
grep '<span>5</span>' pure/index.html
! grep 'function add' pure/index.html

# Without it the call is left alone: nothing infers purity from a body the call
# never reaches, so a stub body cannot fold its own answer into the program.
sngl generate --lang=none --platform=html --out=stub stub.sngl
grep 'function add' stub/index.html
! grep '<span>0</span>' stub/index.html

# async is the same fact the TypeScript importer reads off Promise<T>, so it
# drives the same lowering: the computed that calls it is hoisted behind a
# settled-state field and an async kicker awaits the call. Nothing was imported
# to say so — the mark is the only source of it.
sngl generate --lang=none --platform=html --out=async async.sngl
grep 'async function \$compute___hoist_0' async/index.html
grep 'await fetchHello' async/index.html

# A misspelled flag is a spelling error the compiler can see, so it names the
# alternatives rather than ignoring the flag.
! sngl check typo.sngl
stderr 'unknown value "puer"'
stderr 'async, native'

# Purity is not a flag: it is `const func`, which says so for any function.
! sngl check pureflag.sngl
stderr 'unknown value "pure"'

# The flags describe a call, so a declaration that has none refuses them.
! sngl check onstruct.sngl
stderr 'which describes a call'

# native is the exception, because it describes the declaration rather than a
# call: it says the host already has this, so nothing is emitted for it and a
# reference resolves to the host name. A struct says that as readily as a
# function does.
# Asserted on Go, because a type name is where the difference shows: the
# reference resolves to the host's own name and nothing declares a second one.
sngl generate --lang=go --platform=bubbletea --out=native native.sngl
grep 'api\.Entry' native/model.go
! grep 'type Entry struct' native/model.go

-- pure.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"
import . "sngl:macro"

#[foreign("js:./api", "add")]
const func add(a int, b int) => a + b

component main node {
    text(value=string(add(2, 3)))
}

window {
    main
}
-- stub.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"
import . "sngl:macro"

#[foreign("js:./api", "add")]
func add(a int, b int) => 0

component main node {
    text(value=string(add(2, 3)))
}

window {
    main
}
-- async.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"
import . "sngl:macro"

#[foreign("js:./api", "fetchHello", async)]
func fetchHello(name string) => "hi " + name

func greeting() => fetchHello("world")

component main node {
    text(value=greeting())
}

window {
    main
}
-- typo.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"
import . "sngl:macro"

#[foreign("js:./api", "add", puer)]
func add(a int, b int) => a + b

component main node {
    text(value=string(add(2, 3)))
}

window {
    main
}
-- pureflag.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"
import . "sngl:macro"

#[foreign("js:./api", "add", pure)]
func add(a int, b int) => a + b

component main node {
    text(value=string(add(2, 3)))
}

window {
    main
}
-- onstruct.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"
import . "sngl:macro"

#[foreign("js:./api", "Entry", async)]
struct Entry {
    title string
}

component main node {
    text(value=Entry{title = "x"}.title)
}

window {
    main
}
-- native.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"
import . "sngl:macro"

#[foreign("go:example.com/api", "api.Entry", native)]
struct Entry {
    title string
}

#[foreign("go:example.com/api", "api.Load")]
func load() Entry { return Entry{title = "x"} }

component main node {
    text(value=load().title)
}

window {
    main
}
